title: See what opposite delivery orders do
description: Apply the same two concurrent edits at replicas A and B. The replicas receive the remote edit in opposite orders, exposing whether the selected policy converges and whether accepted intent remains visible.

strategies.label: Whole snapshot, server last-writer-wins
strategies.detail: The authority selects one complete submitted value and distributes it to both replicas.
strategies.principle: This converges through central ordering, but the overwrite boundary is the entire document value.

strategies.label: Raw positions, arrival order
strategies.detail: Each replica applies local and remote positions without transforming them or using stable element identity.
strategies.principle: Delivery order changes the meaning of a position, so receiving the same edits is not enough for convergence.

strategies.label: Typed merge with stable identities
strategies.detail: Sequence inserts use deterministic element identity; incompatible scalar writes retain conflict metadata for review.
strategies.principle: Merge behavior is defined per datatype instead of treating the document as one undifferentiated value.

scenarios.label: Two text inserts at one anchor
scenarios.detail: Both editors add an adjective after the same word while disconnected.

snapshot-overwrite.explanation: Both replicas agree only because the authority keeps B's full snapshot. A's accepted-looking text disappears.

orderA: B inserts fast at the original offset
orderB: A inserts secure at the original offset
raw-offsets.explanation: Both words survive, but each replica's second insert lands before its first. The final text depends on delivery order.

orderA: B element merges at the shared anchor
orderB: A element merges at the shared anchor
typed-stable-merge.explanation: Stable element identities and one deterministic tie-break order make delivery order irrelevant while retaining both inserts.

scenarios.label: Two owners for one task
scenarios.detail: The task schema permits one visible owner, but both editors assign a different person concurrently.

snapshot-overwrite.explanation: The replicas converge, but the overwritten assignment is no longer inspectable. The product cannot explain that a conflict occurred.

raw-offsets.explanation: Each replica accepts the last value it happens to receive, so the same two writes produce different owners.

orderA: B value is retained as concurrent
orderB: A value wins deterministic display order
typed-stable-merge.explanation: Both replicas show the same provisional winner and retain the alternative. A user or domain command must resolve the single-owner invariant.

scenarios.label: Two cards inserted first
scenarios.detail: Both editors add a different task at position zero in the same ordered list.

snapshot-overwrite.explanation: The list converges by replacing all of it. Security disappears even though it was accepted locally.

raw-offsets.explanation: Both cards survive, but applying an index-zero insert second puts it first. The replicas disagree on list order.

orderA: B item merges at the same anchor
orderB: A item merges by stable order
typed-stable-merge.explanation: The sequence datatype orders concurrent identified elements consistently, independent of arrival order.
